_comment: Stage 0 output. Column names below were read from info.csv AND verified against the live CSV headers on HuggingFace. Nothing here is guessed; fields that are NOT shipped and must be derived are marked derived=true.

dataset.name: NUS Global Streetscapes
dataset.note: HuggingFace hosts tabular data only. Imagery is downloaded separately (Stage 2).

provenance.headers_verified: Actual first-line headers of simplemaps.csv, segmentation.csv, osm.csv, metadata_common_attributes.csv, places365.csv and ghsl.csv were fetched via HTTP range request and compared against info.csv.

join_key.explanation: Universally Unique IDentifier, unique for every image. Present in every table.
join_key.secondary_explanation: source is 'Mapillary' or 'KartaView'; orig_id is that platform's own image id.

city.explanation: The name of the city/town as an ASCII string (e.g. Goiania). Left blank if ASCII representation is not possible.
city.use_as: classification label for the Stage 4/5 pretext task

companions.city_id: 10-digit unique id generated by SimpleMaps; stable grouping key, prefer over name string
companions.continent: continent, useful for Stage 1 region spread

assumptions_flagged: city_ascii can be BLANK where no ASCII form exists. Use city_id as the grouping key and city_ascii only as a display/label string.

City attribution comes from SimpleMaps nearest-city matching, not administrative boundaries. An image near a city edge may be labelled with the adjacent city. gadm.csv NAME_1..NAME_5 is the administrative alternative if this proves noisy.

alternatives.note: settlement typology, not a city name

sequence_id.explanation: Sequence ID of the image specified by Mapillary / KartaView
sequence_id.use_as: GROUPING KEY for the train/val split (non-negotiable rule 1). Split by this, never randomly.

companions.sequence_index: int, the order index of the image in its sequence
companions.sequence_img_count: int, number of images available in the sequence

assumptions_flagged: NOT YET VERIFIED: whether sequence_id is globally unique or only unique within a source. If KartaView and Mapillary can collide, the split key must be the pair (source, sequence_id). Stage 1 will check this on the real rows before any split is built.

greenery.explanation: Calculated by dividing 'Vegetation' column by 'Total' column
greenery.use_as: physical attribute for the Stage 7 evaluation metric and the Stage 8 UMAP recolour

companions.Vegetation: int, raw pixel count of the Vegetation semantic class
companions.Total: int, total number of pixels in image
companions.Terrain: int, pixel count of Terrain class - NOT included in green_view_index

assumptions_flagged: green_view_index counts the 'Vegetation' class ONLY. 'Terrain' (grass, soil) is excluded. If a broader greenery definition is wanted, compute (Vegetation + Terrain) / Total instead.

building_density.explanation: NO SHIPPED COLUMN EXISTS for building density. segmentation.csv ships 'Building' (int, number of pixels of that semantic class) and 'Total' (int, total pixels). The ratio is the direct analogue of the shipped green_view_index, which is Vegetation/Total.
building_density.use_as: physical attribute for the Stage 7 evaluation metric
assumptions_flagged: THIS IS A DERIVED COLUMN, NOT A DATASET COLUMN. The dataset has no 'building density' field. We compute Building/Total by analogy with green_view_index.

It measures the building share of the IMAGE, i.e. how built-up the view is, not built-up area per unit ground area. That is a defensible visual-density proxy but it is not the urban-planning definition of building density.

alternatives.note: Number of segmented building INSTANCES in the image - a count, not an area share. Complements the pixel ratio.

GHSL settlement typology at the image LOCATION, not from the image: 30 urban centre, 23 dense urban cluster, 22 semi-dense urban cluster, 21 suburban/peri-urban, 13 rural cluster, 12 low density rural, 11 very low density rural, 10 water. This is the closest thing to a true ground-truth density label.
The GHSL settlement typology term matching urban_code.

road_type.explanation: Type of road associated with the edge (e.g. primary, secondary, residential, footway, cycleway, etc.)
road_type.use_as: categorical physical attribute for the Stage 7 evaluation metric

companions.type_highway: string, coarser grouping: whether the edge is for driving, cycling, walking, or others
companions.lanes: int, number of lanes on the edge
companions.maxspeed: string, speed limit on the edge
companions.oneway: bool, whether the edge is one-way
companions.snap_dist: float, distance from the image to the OSM edge it was snapped to

assumptions_flagged: Both 'highway' (fine-grained) and 'type_highway' (coarse: drive/cycle/walk/other) exist. Use type_highway for the categorical evaluation attribute - 'highway' has a long tail of rare OSM values that would make a per-class metric noisy.
OSM attribution is a spatial SNAP, not ground truth. snap_dist should be checked and a sanity threshold applied in Stage 1; a large snap_dist means the road type may belong to a different street.

forbidden.rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable rule 2 - perception scores are not used anywhere in this project.
forbidden.note: CLAUDE.md refers to these as safety/wealth/beauty/lively/boring/depressing. The ACTUAL column names are the adjectives listed above, capitalised. Recorded here so the loader can explicitly drop them by their real names.

known_documentation_bugs.issue: info.csv documents this table's 4th field as 'Safe' (copy-paste from perception.csv). The ACTUAL header is 'uuid,source,orig_id,place'. The explanation text - 'The type of place or scene classified for the image' - is correct and belongs to the column named 'place'.

tables._comment: All tables live under data/ in the HF repo, as .csv and mirrored as .parquet under data/parquet/. Prefer parquet for load speed.

used_in_this_project.data/metadata_common_attributes.csv: sequence_id split key, lat/lon, datetime, image dims, heading, projection_type
used_in_this_project.cities688.csv: per-city summary WITH an img_count column - the natural starting point for Stage 1 city selection

cities688.note: img_count gives images per city directly, so Stage 1's >=2000-images acceptance check can be pre-screened here without loading the full 10M-row tables.
